title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, optimize cache & job matrix
author: Alex Kim
description:
Motivation: our monolithic GitHub Actions workflow has grown slow and brittle. The combined lint/test/release pipeline runs many unrelated jobs for every PR, increasing queue times and cache contention. This PR splits the combined workflow into focused workflows (lint, test, release), extracts reusable templates, and improves caching and matrix heuristics to reduce CI latency and cost.

Summary of changes: split workflows to .github/workflows/ci-lint.yml, .github/workflows/ci-test.yml and .github/workflows/release.yml; add reusable templates in .github/workflows/.github-reusable/ci-lint.yml and ci-test.yml; improve cache keys (include package-lock hash + node version) and restore semantics to reduce cache misses; add fast-path matrix for PRs (only run full matrix on main or dedicated e2e runs); reduce job concurrency and ensure job-level timeouts; add a release dry-run and stricter approval gating; update docs/ci.md with new workflow guidance.

Checklist: 
- [x] Split workflows and add reusable templates
- [x] Improve cache keys and test cache hit rates in canary
- [x] Add PR-level fast-path matrix
- [x] Update release automation to require token rotation check
- [x] Update docs and notify infra channel

Risk/rollout: non-breaking, rolling out to all repos in the monorepo gradually. The change is gated by preserving the old workflow (old-combined.yml) as a backup for 48 hours and by running release dry-runs. If we see regressions we can roll back by disabling the new workflows.

Notes: this also bumps Node to 20 for CI images for consistency with other infra PRs and consolidates common setup steps into reusable workflows to reduce duplication.
commits: Split workflows into ci-lint.yml, ci-test.yml and release.yml
Extract reusable workflow templates and move helpers to .github/workflows/.github-reusable
Improve cache key and restore logic to include package-lock.json checksum and node version
Add PR fast-path job matrix to reduce concurrent runners on non-main branches
Add release dry-run and token rotation check
Docs: update docs/ci.md and add migration notes
review_comments: Maria Gonzalez: Suggested tightening the cache key to include package-lock hash — implemented in commit 3.
Evan Park: Requested that the full test matrix only run on main and dedicated CI branches; added PR fast-path that runs a reduced matrix and e2e on main via a conditional.
Jordan Lee: Pointed out a potential permission escalation in the release action; added token rotation check and dry-run before merging.
Alex Kim (author): Responded to comments and pushed follow-up commits to address flaky integration tests and the cache restore ordering.
ci_checks: unit tests: initially failed (timeout on worker 3) -> rerun -> pass
integration tests: flaky on first run (external service timeout) -> rerun -> pass
cache hit rate (canary): improved from ~58% to ~88% on subsequent runs
merge_summary: Squashed and merged after approvals from Maria, Evan, and Jordan. CI passed on reruns and a 24h canary showed stable cache behavior and reduced median workflow runtime from ~14m to ~7m for PRs.
release_notes: CI: split monolithic workflow into separate lint/test/release pipelines, improved cache keys and fast-path PR matrix to reduce CI latency and runner costs. No user-facing changes.
notes: Follow-up tasks: rollout similar reusable templates to redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript repos, and schedule a cron to retire old-combined.yml after 48h if no regressions observed.
